# sherpa-data-grid

A sortable, filterable, groupable data table.

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Category | data |
| Figma | Grid Cell |
| Source | [.ts](../../src/components/sherpa-data-grid/sherpa-data-grid.ts) · [.html](../../src/components/sherpa-data-grid/sherpa-data-grid.html) · [.css](../../src/components/sherpa-data-grid/sherpa-data-grid.css) · [.component.json](../../src/components/sherpa-data-grid/sherpa-data-grid.component.json) · [.example.json](../../src/components/sherpa-data-grid/sherpa-data-grid.example.json) |

## When to use it

For a table of records that can be sorted, filtered, grouped and selected. It reports what the reader does, and its host owns the sort, filter, page and selection; for a plain stack of rows, use `sherpa-list`, and for label and value pairs, `sherpa-key-value-list`.

## Example

```html
<div style="block-size: 320px"><sherpa-data-grid data-selectable data-column-filters data-filterable></sherpa-data-grid></div>
```

`populate()` is given, on `sherpa-data-grid`:

```json
{
  "key": "id",
  "columns": [
    {
      "field": "name",
      "header": "Name",
      "sortable": true
    },
    {
      "field": "plan",
      "header": "Plan",
      "sortable": true
    },
    {
      "field": "seats",
      "header": "Seats",
      "type": "number",
      "sortable": true
    }
  ],
  "rows": [
    {
      "id": "a",
      "name": "Ada Lovelace",
      "plan": "Pro",
      "seats": 12
    },
    {
      "id": "b",
      "name": "Grace Hopper",
      "plan": "Free",
      "seats": 3
    },
    {
      "id": "c",
      "name": "Alan Turing",
      "plan": "Team",
      "seats": 8
    }
  ],
  "actions": [
    {
      "id": "edit",
      "label": "Edit",
      "icon": "pencil"
    },
    {
      "id": "delete",
      "label": "Delete",
      "icon": "trash",
      "danger": true,
      "multi": true
    }
  ]
}
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data-apply-on` | `change` `input` |  |  |
| `data-bounds` | text |  |  |
| `data-column-filters` | boolean |  | a filter button in each column heading |
| `data-column-values` | text |  | the WHOLE column's values, so a filter menu offers them all even when the drawn rows carry only some: `field:a\|b\|c` per entry, NEWLINE separated. A value no drawn row carries sorts below a divider, dimmed but still selectable — that is how a reader broadens a filter back out. TRAP T-unavailable-value-sorts-below-a-divider |
| `data-filter-fields` | text |  | space-separated fields an EXTERNAL filter is narrowing; those columns' headings take data-status="active". Written by SherpaDataSource — a host driving the grid by hand can write it too. |
| `data-filterable` | boolean |  | show a secondary header row of filter inputs |
| `data-group-field` | text |  | group rows by this column |
| `data-locked` | boolean |  |  |
| `data-needles` | text |  | what an EXTERNAL filter MATCHED on, so its hits mark in the cells: `field:op:value` per entry, NEWLINE separated. Written by SherpaDataSource beside data-filter-fields. Only substring ops appear — `eq` matched the whole value and `ne` matched by absence, so neither leaves a span to point at. TRAP T-a-needle-comes-from-either-direction |
| `data-page` | number |  | the visual page, WHILE GROUPED only — a page is data-page-size ROWS, and a shut group is one slot. Written by SherpaDataSource; the grid reports back the page count it arrives at and never writes data-page itself. |
| `data-page-size` | number |  | the visual page, WHILE GROUPED only — a page is data-page-size ROWS, and a shut group is one slot. Written by SherpaDataSource; the grid reports back the page count it arrives at and never writes data-page itself. |
| `data-scope` | text |  | ASKED of its provider: the Query scope its headings answer |
| `data-select` | `single` `multiple` | `multiple` | multiple \| single — single draws RADIOS, holds one row, and shows no control in the header: "select all" is meaningless where only one can be chosen |
| `data-selectable` | boolean |  | show a leading selection column |
| `data-sort-direction` | `asc` `desc` `""` |  | current sort (asc \| desc) |
| `data-sort-field` | text |  | current sort (asc \| desc) |
| `data-total-pages` | number |  | how many pages the host believes there are. The grid reads it and never writes it: a Find steps past the last page by it, and a count that has not changed is not reported again, so the echo of its own report cannot loop. JS API — what a person can do by clicking, a caller can do by calling. This is what lets a SAVED VIEW, a preset or an agent configure a grid: setColumnFilter(field, clause) set one column's filter from a store FilterClause columnClause(field) read it back — the same clause, for saving suspendColumnFilter(field, on) keep the clause but stop applying it clearColumnFilter(field?) delete one, or all openColumnFilter(field, anchor) open that column's menu, anchored anywhere select(keys) / clearSelection() set the selection BY KEY (needs `key` in populate) actionsFor(count) the actions that apply to a selection of that size — all of them for 1, only the `multi` ones for 2+, none for 0. A bulk toolbar reads this so it cannot disagree with the row menu selectedKeys / selectedRecords read it back |

## Methods

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `drawPresent(present: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>)` | drawPresent(present, scope) — a bound source says what the filters before each field leave; a heading's menu greys the rest. A field not named is not limited. |
| `drawOffered(offered: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>)` | drawOffered(offered) — what each serial-set field OFFERS: a heading's menu removes the rest, but keeps a pick. |
| `setColumnFilter(field: string, clause: unknown[] \| null)` | Set one column's filter from OUTSIDE. — SILENT, and takes the clause `column-filter-change` reports. |
| `supersedeColumns(readings: Readonly<Record<string, FieldReading>>, appliedAt?: string)` | supersedeColumns(readings, appliedAt) — the fields a HIGHER scope holds, each with the answer it holds there. A named heading SHOWS that answer, read-only, with the superseded look and tip, so no contradicting pick can be made in it; a heading not named is released. Will, 2026-09-26. |
| `columnClause(field: string)` | One column's filter as a ready FilterClause, or null. — a SUSPENDED clause is returned too. |
| `columnReading(field: string)` | One column's filter as a READING, or null — what a saved view set on it. |
| `drawReading(field: string, reading: FieldReading)` | drawReading(field, reading) — a bound source tells this grid one column's answer, whoever set it: a chip, the panel, a restored Query. SILENT. |
| `columnLabel(field: string)` | One column filter AS A READER SEES IT — "Contains: ana", "Is not: churned". |
| `suspendColumnFilter(field: string, suspended = true)` | Suspend or resume, never lose. . |
| `openColumnFilter(field: string, anchor?: HTMLElement)` | Open one column's filter menu, anchored where the caller says. — one menu serves both. |
| `clearColumnFilter(field?: string)` | Drop one column's heading filter from OUTSIDE; nothing drops them all. . |
| `findStep(direction: 1 \| -1 = 1)` | findStep(direction) — move to the next or previous MATCH, and show it. Past this page's last it asks for the next page (`page-change`) and lands on its first; before the first, the previous page's last — round from the end to the start, as a browser's own find. Answers where it is on this page: `{ index, count }`, `index` -1 while a page loads. |
| `actionsFor(count: number)` | The actions for the CURRENT selection — one row: all; two or more: only `multi`. . |
| `neighbour(by: number)` | The row `by` rows from the current one, in the order drawn — or null. |
| `stepCurrent(by: number)` | Move the current row `by` rows. Silent; returns the new one, or null at an end. |
| `select(keys: readonly string[])` | Select exactly these rows, by key. — REPLACES, ignores unmatched keys, and is SILENT. `select([])` clears. |
| `clearSelection()` | Select nothing. The same as `select([])`, said plainly. |

## Events

Each one bubbles.

| Event | Detail | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| `column-resize` | `{ field: string; width: number \| undefined }` |  |
| `sort-change` | `{ direction: SortDirection \| null; field: null \| string }` |  |
| `row-select` | `{ index: number; row: GridRow \| undefined }` |  |
| `selection-change` | `{ records: GridRow[]; selected: string[] }` |  |
| `column-filter-change` | `{ clause: null \| unknown[]; field: string; from: null \| string; header: string; label: null \| string; op: null \| string; reading: object; to: null \| string; value: null \| string }` |  |
| `filter-change` | `{ field: string; filters: { [k: string]: string; }; value: string; visible: number }` |  |
| `group-toggle` | `{ collapsed: boolean; value: string }` |  |
| `row-action` | `{ id: string; records: GridRow[] }` | An action was chosen, from the row menu or a host's bulk bar. |
| `page-change` | `{ page: number }` | A Find stepped past this page's first or last match: a REQUEST for the page it goes on to |
| `grid-pages-change` | `{ page: number; pages: number }` | How many pages the CURRENT fold state makes, while grouped. |
| `select-all-request` | `{ answer: (rows: readonly GridRow[]) => void }` | "Select all rows" while its source pages: a REQUEST for every matching row, answered through answer(rows). A host may call `preventDefault()` to take it over. |
